summary: Emergency safe drain and reallocate: quantized batching + KV cache tuning causing per-tenant tail latency
description: Issue summary: After applying a tenant-scoped optimizer profile that enabled aggressive int8 quantization + async batching + KV prefetch for gptj-8b-int8, LumeHealth is seeing intermittent 95/99p tail latency spikes (1.2s -> 5–7s) on a subset (~12%) of inference requests. Impact: Customer-facing API timeouts and degraded user experience for multi-turn chat flows. No error 5xx spike, but significant latency augmentation for many sessions. Environment: Production (dedicated pool), us-east region, tenant_id=lh-prod-7. Recent change: Optimizer profile rollout on 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC via console staged rollout (20% -> 100% over 2h).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Authenticate as tenant lh-prod-7 and send standard multi-turn chat payload (system + 3 user turns).
2) Observe streaming latency and tail completion times across 1000 requests (via smoke harness).
3) Compare with baseline profile (no async batching / conservative quantization).
4) Reproduce easiest on sequences with variable prompt lengths (avg token len 120).

comments: 2026-03-10 01:05 UTC - Diego Martinez (Support): Acknowledged. Initial hypothesis: async batching bump + KV prefetch is creating uneven scheduling pressure for variable-length prompts. Opening SRE runbook and paging scheduler-oncall.

2026-03-10 01:20 UTC - SRE (Priya Rao): Observed elevated queue depth on a subset of workers pinned to tenant lh-prod-7. No GPU OOMs. Suggest draining affected workers, disabling async batching for the tenant, and falling back to sync batching + conservative quant profile as a safe rollback.

2026-03-10 01:47 UTC - Support (Diego Martinez): Action plan sent to customer: perform controlled drain, apply fallback profile (opt-tenant-lh-prod-7-safe) which sets int8->fp16 mixed mode and async_batch_size=1, disable kv-prefetch. Awaiting customer approval to proceed at 02:00 UTC.
2026-03-10 02:14 UTC - LumeHealth (Sara Patel): Approved. Please proceed and confirm when finished.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Aggressive int8 path combined with async batch packing causes higher variance in per-token kernel selection and longer tail in scheduler pack/unpack, amplified when KV prefetch misses are non-uniform across session lengths.

Checked GPU perf counters on affected worker pool: sustained SM utilization OK, but scheduler lock contention spikes correlate with tail latency windows (see perf trace link: https://perf.redwood.com/trace/trace-7721).
Verified that the staged rollout increased impact as percent rolled to 100% — latency deviation curve matches the rollout window.

Temporary mitigation options considered: (A) instant profile rollback (global) - disruptive; (B) per-tenant safe fallback - less disruptive; (C) surgical worker drain + selective rollback - targets fewer customers.
Chosen path: per-tenant safe fallback + surgical drain of 6 affected workers, then monitor 95/99p for 2 hours before rolling to other tenants if stable.
resolution: Workaround applied 2026-03-10 02:35 UTC: Console staged action 'applyFallbackProfile' executed for tenant lh-prod-7. Fallback profile details: quant_mode=mixed_fp16, async_batching=off, kv_prefetch=off, batch_timeout_ms=10.
Surgical drain executed for 6 workers pinned to tenant; traffic rebalanced to healthy pool. Observed 95p latency drop from ~5.2s to ~520ms within 12 minutes after change.
Post-change monitoring: 6-hour rolling dashboard shows no 99p spikes >1.0s for tenant. Customer confirmed UX restored.

Follow-up actions: (1) Create a test harness for variable-length prompts vs async batching (owner: QA perf team, due 2026-03-17). (2) Add a preflight validation check in console: detect kv-prefetch miss_ratio > 30% before enabling aggressive optimizer profiles (owner: Console team, due 2026-03-24). (3) Add a documented emergency 'tenant safe-fallback' button in runbook (owner: SRE, due 2026-03-20).
Status: Mitigated and monitoring. Keep ticket open until postmortem and runbook updates completed.
Related PRs for permanent fix: runtime PR #2486 (improve kernel selection under async batching) and scheduler PR #1021 (reduce lock contention during pack/unpack).
